newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Wall St losses depress S.African shares at close.
newsitem.headline: Wall St losses depress S.African shares at close.

text.p: A weaker than expected start on Wall Street pressured South African shares, dragging them off ground they struggled to win after the morning's slide to finish softer on the day, dealers said.
"We were pulled down on the back of the Dow Jones. It opened lower than everyone thought and there is a lot of downward pressure," one dealer said.
Shares opened weaker, largely led by futures-related trade, but the market recovered in later trade, supported by strong bond and rand rates, ahead of the U.S. market's opening.
With U.S. markets closed on Monday for the Labour Day public holiday, dealers said Wall Street's losses could dampen local trade early next week in the absence of other fresh factors.
Dealers said trade had been active with much foreign interest throughout the day.
"It was a busy day with 43 million shares changing hands, value of about 482 million rand," one dealer said.
The overall index was off 15.1 points at 6,688.9, industrials were off 18.6 points to 7,835.2 and golds fell 21.1 to 1,787.6.
